+#pragma once
+
+#include <functional>
+#include <optional>
+
+#include "drake/bindings/pydrake/pydrake_pybind.h"
+#include "drake/systems/framework/context.h"
+#include "drake/systems/framework/event.h"
+#include "drake/systems/framework/event_status.h"
+#include "drake/systems/framework/system.h"
+
+namespace drake {
+namespace pydrake {
+
+/* Because Python doesn't offer static type checking to help remind the user to
+return an EventStatus from an event handler function, we'll bind the callback
+as optional<> to allow the user to omit a return statement. (When declaring a
+periodic event in C++, the user-provided callback function is similarly
+overloaded to return either EventStatus or void. We can't overload based on
+return values in pybind11, so that's another reason we'll use optional<> in
+Python for the same effect.) */
+template <typename... Args>
+using CppEventSignature = std::optional<systems::EventStatus>(Args...);
+
+/* Declare the handler signature within std::function. */
+template <typename... Args>
+using CppEventCallback = std::function<CppEventSignature<Args...>>;
+
+/* Declare the handler signature as a python function object with compile-time
+readable type signature. */
+#ifdef PYDRAKE_USE_PYBIND11
+template <typename... Args>
+using PyEventCallback = py::typing::Callable<CppEventSignature<Args...>>;
+#else   // PYDRAKE_USE_NANOBIND
+template <typename... Args>
+using PyEventCallback = py::typed<py::callable, CppEventSignature<Args...>>;
+#endif  // PYDRAKE_USE_PYBIND11
+
+/* Declare the various callback types that will appear as parameters of
+bindings, such that automatic documentation has correct type signatures. Each
+PyFooCallback is paired with a CppFooCallback that has the identical argument
+list, so that bindings can always py::cast from PyFooCallback<T> to
+CppFooCallback<T> without needing to cross-check argument alignment. */
+
+// For LeafSystem::Declare{Initialization,Periodic,PerStep,Forced}*Event.
+template <typename T>
+using PyPublishCallback = PyEventCallback<const systems::Context<T>*>;
+template <typename T>
+using CppPublishCallback = CppEventCallback<const systems::Context<T>*>;
+
+template <typename T>
+using PyDiscreteUpdateCallback =
+    PyEventCallback<const systems::Context<T>*, systems::DiscreteValues<T>*>;
+template <typename T>
+using CppDiscreteUpdateCallback =
+    CppEventCallback<const systems::Context<T>*, systems::DiscreteValues<T>*>;
+
+template <typename T>
+using PyUnrestrictedUpdateCallback =
+    PyEventCallback<const systems::Context<T>*, systems::State<T>*>;
+template <typename T>
+using CppUnrestrictedUpdateCallback =
+    CppEventCallback<const systems::Context<T>*, systems::State<T>*>;
+
+// For the PublishEvent and UnrestrictedUpdateEvent constructors.
+template <typename T>
+using PyPublishEventCallback = PyEventCallback<const systems::Context<T>*,
+    const systems::PublishEvent<T>*>;
+template <typename T>
+using CppPublishEventCallback = CppEventCallback<const systems::Context<T>*,
+    const systems::PublishEvent<T>*>;
+
+template <typename T>
+using PyPublishEventSystemCallback = PyEventCallback<const systems::System<T>*,
+    const systems::Context<T>*, const systems::PublishEvent<T>*>;
+template <typename T>
+using CppPublishEventSystemCallback =
+    CppEventCallback<const systems::System<T>*, const systems::Context<T>*,
+        const systems::PublishEvent<T>*>;
+
+template <typename T>
+using PyUnrestrictedUpdateEventCallback =
+    PyEventCallback<const systems::Context<T>*,
+        const systems::UnrestrictedUpdateEvent<T>*, systems::State<T>*>;
+template <typename T>
+using CppUnrestrictedUpdateEventCallback =
+    CppEventCallback<const systems::Context<T>*,
+        const systems::UnrestrictedUpdateEvent<T>*, systems::State<T>*>;
+
+template <typename T>
+using PyUnrestrictedUpdateEventSystemCallback =
+    PyEventCallback<const systems::System<T>*, const systems::Context<T>*,
+        const systems::UnrestrictedUpdateEvent<T>*, systems::State<T>*>;
+template <typename T>
+using CppUnrestrictedUpdateEventSystemCallback =
+    CppEventCallback<const systems::System<T>*, const systems::Context<T>*,
+        const systems::UnrestrictedUpdateEvent<T>*, systems::State<T>*>;
+
+}  // namespace pydrake
+}  // namespace drake

+#pragma once
+
+#include <string>
+
+#include "drake/bindings/pydrake/common/ref_cycle_pybind.h"
+#include "drake/bindings/pydrake/pydrake_pybind.h"
+
+namespace drake {
+namespace pydrake {
+namespace internal {
+
+/* internal::ensure_callback_lifetime is a custom call policy for pydrake.
+
+For an overview of other call policies, See
+https://pybind11.readthedocs.io/en/stable/advanced/functions.html#additional-call-policies
+https://nanobind.readthedocs.io/en/latest/functions.html#lifetime-annotations
+
+`ensure_callback_lifetime` creates a one-way reference from an arbitrary object
+to a Python callable object that Python's garbage collection can track. Even
+though the immediately constructed reference is one-way, compatibility with
+garbage collection is necessary to handle callables that capture Python
+variables and thereby create reference cycles.
+
+This policy uses the same underlying technique and implementation as
+pydrake::internal::ref_cycle. Python callable objects need special lifetime
+treatment because (1) they cannot in general participate directly in a
+pydrake::internal::ref_cycle, and (2) even tracking their identities requires
+special handling.
+
+For the special case of binding custom constructors, the
+ensure-callback-lifetime treatment can only be applied as a call policy. This
+is because casting `self` to python inside a custom constructor lambda "works"
+in an unexpected way: it creates a python "temporary" that is immediately
+discarded, and that is unrelated to the completed instance ultimately delivered
+to the calling python code.
+
+Note the consequences for object lifetimes:
+
+* Nurse keeps CallbackPatient alive.
+* If the reference forms part of a cycle via captures:
+  * the cycle can be garbage collected once all member objects are unreachable.
+
+@tparam Nurse an argument index to a `ref_cycle` compatible object
+@tparam CallbackPatient an argument index to a callable
+
+The argument index starts at 1; for methods, `self` is at index 1. Index 0
+denotes the return value. */
+template <size_t Nurse, size_t CallbackPatient>
+struct ensure_callback_lifetime {};
+
+/* This function is used in the template below to select participants by
+call/return index. */
+void ensure_callback_lifetime_impl(size_t nurse, size_t callback_patient,
+    const CallInfo& info, py::handle ret);
+
+// For nanobind annotations, we must provide ADL hooks for func_extra_info.
+#ifdef PYDRAKE_USE_NANOBIND
+template <size_t NArgs, size_t Nurse, size_t CallbackPatient>
+NB_INLINE void process_precall(PyObject** args,
+    std::integral_constant<size_t, NArgs>, nanobind::detail::cleanup_list*,
+    ensure_callback_lifetime<Nurse, CallbackPatient>*) {
+  if constexpr (!needs_return_value<Nurse, CallbackPatient>()) {
+    ensure_callback_lifetime_impl(
+        Nurse, CallbackPatient, {args, NArgs}, nanobind::handle());
+  }
+}
+
+template <size_t NArgs, size_t Nurse, size_t CallbackPatient>
+void process_postcall(PyObject** args, std::integral_constant<size_t, NArgs>,
+    PyObject* result, ensure_callback_lifetime<Nurse, CallbackPatient>*) {
+  if constexpr (needs_return_value<Nurse, CallbackPatient>()) {
+    // result_guard avoids leaking a reference to the return object if postcall
+    // throws an exception.
+    py::object result_guard = py::steal(result);
+    ensure_callback_lifetime_impl(
+        Nurse, CallbackPatient, {args, NArgs}, result);
+    result_guard.release();
+  }
+}
+
+template <typename F, size_t Nurse, size_t CallbackPatient>
+NB_INLINE void func_extra_apply(
+    F& f, ensure_callback_lifetime<Nurse, CallbackPatient>, size_t&) {
+  f.flags |=
+      static_cast<uint32_t>(nanobind::detail::func_flags::can_mutate_args);
+}
+#endif  // PYDRAKE_USE_NANOBIND
+
+}  // namespace internal
+}  // namespace pydrake
+}  // namespace drake
+
+namespace PYDRAKE_BINDER_NAMESPACE {
+namespace detail {
+
+// Provide specializations of the internal templates for call policies; this
+// allows writing an annotation that works seamlessly in bindings definitions.
+#ifdef PYDRAKE_USE_PYBIND11
+template <size_t Nurse, size_t CallbackPatient>
+class process_attribute<
+    drake::pydrake::internal::ensure_callback_lifetime<Nurse, CallbackPatient>>
+    : public process_attribute_default<drake::pydrake::internal::
+              ensure_callback_lifetime<Nurse, CallbackPatient>> {
+ public:
+  // NOLINTNEXTLINE(runtime/references)
+  static void precall(function_call& call) {
+    if constexpr (!needs_return_value_) {
+      drake::pydrake::internal::ensure_callback_lifetime_impl(
+          Nurse, CallbackPatient, {call}, handle());
+    }
+  }
+
+  // NOLINTNEXTLINE(runtime/references)
+  static void postcall(function_call& call, handle ret) {
+    if constexpr (needs_return_value_) {
+      drake::pydrake::internal::ensure_callback_lifetime_impl(
+          Nurse, CallbackPatient, {call}, ret);
+    }
+  }
+
+ private:
+  static constexpr bool needs_return_value_ =
+      drake::pydrake::internal::needs_return_value<Nurse, CallbackPatient>();
+};
+#else   // PYDRAKE_USE_NANOBIND
+template <size_t Nurse, size_t CallbackPatient, typename... Ts>
+struct func_extra_info<
+    drake::pydrake::internal::ensure_callback_lifetime<Nurse, CallbackPatient>,
+    Ts...> : func_extra_info<Ts...> {
+  static constexpr bool pre_post_hooks = true;
+};
+#endif  // PYDRAKE_USE_PYBIND11
+
+}  // namespace detail
+}  // namespace PYDRAKE_BINDER_NAMESPACE

+from pydrake.systems.framework import (
+    LeafSystem,
+    PublishEvent,
+    TriggerType,
+    UnrestrictedUpdateEvent,
+    WitnessFunctionDirection,
+)
+
+
+def DeclareAllEvents(system, get_callback):
+    """Declares one of every kind of event on the given system. Calls
+    get_callback() anew for every declaration to obtain the callback; see
+    MethodLeafSystem for why that matters.
+    """
+
+    def make_event_objects():
+        # Always returns new objects, so that no event object is ever passed
+        # to more than one declaration.
+        return [
+            PublishEvent(get_callback()),
+            PublishEvent(system_callback=get_callback()),
+            PublishEvent(TriggerType.kUnknown, get_callback()),
+            PublishEvent(TriggerType.kUnknown, system_callback=get_callback()),
+            UnrestrictedUpdateEvent(get_callback()),
+            UnrestrictedUpdateEvent(system_callback=get_callback()),
+        ]
+
+    for event in make_event_objects():
+        system.DeclareInitializationEvent(event)
+    system.DeclareInitializationPublishEvent(get_callback())
+    system.DeclareInitializationDiscreteUpdateEvent(get_callback())
+    system.DeclareInitializationUnrestrictedUpdateEvent(get_callback())
+
+    for event in make_event_objects():
+        system.DeclarePeriodicEvent(1.0, 0.5, event)
+    system.DeclarePeriodicPublishEvent(1.0, 0.5, get_callback())
+    system.DeclarePeriodicDiscreteUpdateEvent(1.0, 0.5, get_callback())
+    system.DeclarePeriodicUnrestrictedUpdateEvent(1.0, 0.5, get_callback())
+
+    for event in make_event_objects():
+        system.DeclarePerStepEvent(event)
+    system.DeclarePerStepPublishEvent(get_callback())
+    system.DeclarePerStepDiscreteUpdateEvent(get_callback())
+    system.DeclarePerStepUnrestrictedUpdateEvent(get_callback())
+
+    system.DeclareForcedPublishEvent(get_callback())
+    system.DeclareForcedDiscreteUpdateEvent(get_callback())
+    system.DeclareForcedUnrestrictedUpdateEvent(get_callback())
+
+    # Witness functions are never evaluated by these tests (the system does
+    # not report them via DoGetWitnessFunctions), but storing them on the
+    # system forms the reference cycles we want to check.
+    direction = WitnessFunctionDirection.kCrossesZero
+    system._witnesses = [
+        system.MakeWitnessFunction("calc", direction, get_callback()),
+    ] + [
+        system.MakeWitnessFunction("event", direction, get_callback(), event)
+        for event in make_event_objects()
+    ]
